title: performance: add automated canary detection & rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Evan Sullivan
description: Motivation: continuous performance regressions during model rollouts are a major source of user-visible latency spikes and cost regressions. This PR adds automated canary detection for latency and throughput regressions and wires detected regressions into Redwood rollout guards so we can automatically pause/rollback risky rollouts. --- Summary of changes: 1) perf-canary service: new metrics windowing and delta-detection algorithm (percentile-aware, baseline control windows) + configuration for dynamic thresholds; 2) integrations: rollout guard webhook that calls the deployment controller to pause/cancel canary rollouts when thresholds are breached; 3) observability: new Grafana dashboards and perf canary traces; 4) tests: unit tests for detection logic, e2e canary simulation that injects latency/throughput anomalies; 5) ops: new Linear tasks and runbook for investigating triggered guards. --- Why this approach: previous manual alerts were noisy and required human intervention; automated detection with short, configurable cooldowns reduces MTTR and prevents degraded model versions from reaching full traffic. The detection algorithm favors robust percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and uses smoothed baseline windows to avoid spurious rollbacks during expected variance. --- Backwards compatibility: rollout guard integration is opt-in via canary.policy.auto_pause=true. No breaking API changes. --- Rollout plan: merge to main, staged deployment to perf-canary namespace, follow-on monitoring for 72h with human override enabled. --- Related: ENG-1284, ENG-1291, SUP-542.
